title: BBQ Chicken Bowls
shortDescription: Built bowls, big flavor, one line
subtitle: Built bowls, big flavor, one line
description: Built bowls, big flavor, one line. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for BBQ Chicken Bowls in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.instruction: Rinse rice until water runs clear. Simmer with 1:1.5 rice-to-water ratio and salt 18 minutes; fluff and hold covered at 200°F. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill the chicken thighs
steps.instruction: Season chicken thighs with BBQ rub. Grill over medium-high 5–7 minutes per side until char marks show and thickest part reads 165°F. Rest 5 minutes; slice into strips.

steps.title: Warm the BBQ sauce
steps.instruction: Warm BBQ sauce in a small pot over low heat — do not boil or sugars scorch. Keep a ladle on the line. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion BBQ Chicken Bowls onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Scale for larger halls
steps.instruction: When cooking for more than 8 firefighters, split into two pans halfway through so the bottom layer does not overcook while the top waits — duplicate mise en place if you double batches.

steps.title: Build the bowls
steps.instruction: Base of rice, sliced BBQ chicken, corn, and a pile of coleslaw on top for crunch. Drizzle extra sauce on the side. BBQ Chicken Bowls move fastest when hot and cold components are in separate pans.

steps.title: Final quality check before service
steps.instruction: Walk the line once before opening service for BBQ Chicken Bowls — confirm hotel pans are labeled, backup trays are in the 200°F oven, and thermometers are calibrated. Rookies should ask a senior cook to spot-check the first portion.

proTips: Glaze sauce at the end so it doesn't burn on the grill.
Keep slaw on ice under the counter.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Set rice or grain in the first pan, main in the second, crunchy toppings last so textures stay distinct.
Put hot components closest to the crew, cold crunch at the far end of the line.
Line up BBQ Chicken Bowls on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Built bowls, big flavor, one line. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
mealPrepNotes: Prep mise en place before the shift — BBQ Chicken Bowls runs smoother when proteins are trimmed, spices are pre-measured, and hotel pans are labeled before the first tone.
